name: Hybrid 2x Full Body + 2x GPP Fat Loss
dayOfWeek
column17: notes

Low (30 deg) incline on the Smith machine (or dumbbells): both stabilise the lever during the diet. Lower to the upper chest for a full stretch. Two-set method: set 1 at 1 RIR, set 2 at 0-1 RIR. If set 1 lands at the bottom of the rep range, drop the load 5-10% for set 2. In the last weeks of a deep deficit do ONE hard set.

Weighted pull-up, neutral grip, rotate every 3 weeks. Too heavy to start? Use the assisted machine, a band or a lat pulldown and reduce assistance as bodyweight drops (e.g. 60 kg assist to 8 clean reps unassisted, then add weight). Full hang at the bottom, no swinging.
No axial load on the spine (hack squat or Hatfield squat also fine). Objective quad strength tracking regardless of bodyweight. No 1RM testing in the deficit.
Controlled lowering, full range. A banded or ring leg curl works at home. Set 2 at 0 RIR.
Seated anterior delt press: removes trunk stabilisation demands in a deficit. Elbows slightly forward, bar down to the collarbone.
Chest-supported (or inverted row): spares the lower back before Thursday.
Lu raise (or cable lateral raise), scapular plane with a slight forward lean. Safe to go to failure.
Preacher curl with dumbbell or EZ bar. Biceps strength is a reliable marker that muscle is being kept. In the last weeks 1 set.
Dual-rope pushdown. Run 4A-4B-4C as a triplet or finish with the biceps/triceps pair.
SIMPLE 6 circuit, 3 rounds, no rest between exercises (heaviest to lightest), 3 min rest between rounds. Halve the reps (5/10) if needed. Pull-up, 10 reps in the circuit. Assisted version if needed.
Parallel-bar dips, 20 reps (or halve to 10).
Underhand chin-up. If failure comes early use 15-30 s rest-pause and finish the set.
Diamond push-ups.
Inverted row.
Narrow push-ups.
Light plate on the forehead or neck harness, fully controlled. Without direct work the neck loses 2.5-5 cm during a diet.
Light, full range, no jerking.
Leg raises (or decline sit-ups) for the abdominal wall. Not to absolute failure.
Red mini-band, 100 reps total (3 x 33), far from failure: tendon blood flow for elbows. Build up to 200-300 reps if elbows are chronic.
Passive hang from a bar for shoulder decompression.

Gym rings adapt well to the lever changes of a diet. Deficit/weighted ring push-ups, deep dips or a floor press are alternatives. 1-2 s pause in the stretch. Two-set method: set 1 at 1 RIR, set 2 at 0-1 RIR. If set 1 lands at the bottom of the rep range, drop the load 5-10% for set 2. In the last weeks of a deep deficit do ONE hard set.
Diagonal (sagittal) pulldown or underhand ring chin-ups: hits the lower lats without overlapping Monday's wide grip.
Replaces the heavy deadlift: hinge to ~45 deg like an RDL, about 60% of RDL load with far lower systemic fatigue. Barbell or SSB. 1-2 RIR on set 1, 1 RIR on set 2.
Rectus femoris in the stretch (or pendulum sissy / split squat). No extra spinal load after the good mornings. Hold a support.
Full controlled stretch and hard squeeze (home chest crusher also works). Safe to failure.
Seated cable row or chest-expander pull-aparts: upper back and rear delts, protects the shoulders from pressing.
Hammer curl spares the elbows and hits brachialis/forearms; swap to incline curl after 6-8 weeks. In the last weeks 1 set.
Decline dumbbell extension or overhead rope extension for the long head. Follows Monday's pushdowns, which protects the elbows.
30-45 min uphill treadmill walk, zone 2 (or easy cycling or swimming). Purely concentric: costs energy, not recovery, so Monday stays fresh after 96 h.
Dumbbells or a dip belt, no spinal load, full stretch at the bottom.
20-35% of normal load, far from failure with a dynamic swing: opens the discs and flushes the lower back.
100 total reps (3 x 33 or 4 x 25) with cable or band for rear delts and external rotators.
45-60 s holds (or Russian twists, 15-20 reps).
